data.name: Kripanand
data.gender_notes: Kripanand is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Kripa: grace, favor, divine protection; Anand: joy, happiness. The name Kripanand means 'God's gift of joy' or 'God's favor leading to happiness'. The name Kripanand carries the meaning “God's gift” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kripanand usually hope their child will grow to embody god's gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Kripanand belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's gift.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kripanand total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kripanand bears ancient cultural significance in Hinduism, reflecting the rich Indian heritage and philosophical values of grace and joy. Kripanand, as a term, has resonated throughout the centuries in Hindu texts and scriptures, connoting a profound connection with the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Kripanand lies in its meaningful reminder of one's dependence on the divine grace and blessings for happiness and joy in life. This name encourages an attitude of surrender and faith, inviting the recipient to acknowledge the divine as the ultimate source of all joy and happiness. Kripanand serves as a daily reminder to cherish and be grateful for the blessings bestowed upon us by the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kripanand: God's Bliss in the Sword of Action. A name that embodies the warrior spirit, symbolizing the inner battle between the self and the ego, with the sword of action serving as a tool to cut through spiritual illusions.

vedic_reference.note: Kripānand is derived from the Sanskrit word 'कृपा' (Kripa) which means compassionate and merciful. The name is a combination of 'कृप' (Kripa) and 'नन्द' (Nand), where 'नन्द' (Nand) refers to the supreme God, Vishnu, who is known to be the giver of all pleasures and grants boons to his devotees.

historical_references.reference: Kripanand was a 16th century Nath yogi and poet. He is considered one of the most prominent Nath yogis in the lineage of Gorakhnath.
Kripanand was also a renowned scholar and philosopher of the Bhakti movement in India. He is known for his works in Sanskrit and Bengali languages, particularly his commentary on the Bhagavad Gita.
historical_references.context: Scholar and Philosopher of Bhakti Movement
